messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — PRIVATE CONNECTIVITY: High error rate on customer-cx-17 private endpoints (us-west2 AZ subset). Auto-detected 30% packet loss on peering tunnels. Severity: P1.

alex (oncall): acked. Paging now. I’m on it. any quick context?

samir (sre): seeing 502/504s from healthchecks to private endpoints for cust id 17. Affects only requests routed via us-west2-b. Other AZs look OK.

maya (eng-network): joining. I’m pulling BGP/route tables for their VPC peering and our PrivateConnect gateways.

lee (eng-runtime): customer reported failing model inferences through private endpoint, retrying gives 504. No app-level errors in logs yet — looks networky.

maya (eng-network): initial check: one of the BGP tunnels to the cust edge is flapping. Peer AS 64510, local ASN 65100. BGP holdreset seen.

maya (eng-network): running traceroute -> shows asymmetry: inbound traffic to us-west2-b is coming via tunnel A, return path is going via tunnel B which is blackholed intermittently.

maya (eng-network): traceroute snippet:

```
traceroute to 10.0.45.12 (10.0.45.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.2.1.1  0.52 ms  0.50 ms  0.48 ms
 2  192.0.2.45  1.20 ms  1.18 ms  1.16 ms
 3  * * *
 4  * * *
```

maya (eng-network): and BGP neigh show:

```
Neighbor 203.0.113.2  AS 64510  Status: idle (connect-retry)
Neighbor 203.0.113.6  AS 64510  Status: established
```

samir (sre): so partial mesh. Some traffic gets through, others get stuck — consistent with customer reports of intermittent failures.

alex (oncall): impact: P1, customer-facing inference endpoints degraded for subset of traffic (private connectivity only). Multiple customers on same PrivateConnect gateway? Only cust 17 shows healthcheck failures so far.

jess (acct-mgr): I’ve messaged the customer via email and DM: short note that we’re investigating network flap on their private link and working on mitigation. Will follow up with ETA and a workaround.

cloud-support-bot: Support case opened with provider: Case# 1234567890. Provided BGP logs and traceroutes. Engaged network ops.

maya (eng-network): immediate mitigation plan: 1) remove route propagation on the problematic VGW route table so we can manually control advertised paths (temporary), 2) prefer the healthy tunnel by adjusting local preference via BGP community if provider supports, 3) clear conntrack on our NAT/ingress for affected AZ to avoid stuck flows.

samir (sre): I’ll prepare a short runbook for rollback. If any change makes things worse, revert route propagation in 5 mins.

alex (oncall): go for step 1. Keep me posted.

maya (eng-network): executing step 1 — disabling route propagation on rtb-priv-gw-17 for us-west2-b.

incident-bot: Deploy bot: route-table update applied by maya at commit 7f3b2a — no errors.

maya (eng-network): applied BGP policy to prefer 203.0.113.6 (healthy peer) via community set on our side. If this holds, traffic should be symmetric via tunnel6.

samir (sre): running conntrack flush on ingress gateways in us-west2-b.

lee (eng-runtime): I’m restarting the edge proxy in us-west2-b to reset long-lived sockets.

maya (eng-network): quick check: packet loss dropped from 30% -> 2% across the board for affected IPs. Healthchecks starting to green up.

jess (acct-mgr): updated customer: we applied a temporary routing adjustment; they should see improvement. Asking them to confirm.

customer-alert-bot: Customer reported: "Traffic improving, some requests still 5-10% errors."

alex (oncall): acceptable for now but keep working. Who’s owning escalation with cloud provider?

cloud-support-bot: Provider assigned engineer Zoe. They see internal fabric maintenance coincident with BGP reconvergence on us-west2-b. Provider suggests their route-reflector had a race during maintenance, causing one BGP session to drop. Case# 1234567890 -> updated.

maya (eng-network): provider proposed fix: full BGP session reset from provider side + apply jittered hold timers. They asked us to keep both tunnels up while they flip. I asked them to do the reset during a low-traffic minute.

alex (oncall): schedule reset now. Samir, coordinate with provider for reset window and guard rails.

samir (sre): scheduled immediate reset. Will monitor metrics and abort if errors spike >10% within 2 mins.

incident-bot: Provider initiated BGP reset at 1824508590.

maya (eng-network): BGP sessions re-established on both peers: 203.0.113.2 -> established, 203.0.113.6 -> established. Route tables converged.

samir (sre): healthchecks report 99.9% success for private endpoints now. No significant error spikes post-reset.

jess (acct-mgr): customer confirmation: "All good now, thanks for the fast response." They requested an RCA and timeline.

alex (oncall): handoff: I’m going offline for short break. Maya you take lead for postmortem and cloud follow-up? Tag me in the RCA draft.

maya (eng-network): taking lead. I’ll collect BGP dumps, traceroutes, provider logs. Tentative RCA: provider route-reflector maintenance + BGP race caused one of our tunnels to be preferred incorrectly -> asymmetric routing -> intermittent packet loss and healthcheck failures.

lee (eng-runtime): I’ll collect application logs correlated to the incident window and attach to the RCA.

jess (acct-mgr): I’ll follow up with customer with initial incident summary and timeline.

maya (eng-network): long-term mitigations proposed: 1) add active health-checks on BGP neighbors and automated local-preference failover, 2) expand redundant peering across more AZs/providers, 3) add automated conntrack drain on route changes.

samir (sre): scheduling a post-incident review tomorrow 15:00 UTC. Add stakeholders: eng-network, eng-runtime, SRE, support, acct.

alex (oncall): thanks team. I’m handing to maya for now. Back at 1824512000 for RCA review. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident annotated: status -> monitoring. Tags: privateconnect, bgp, asymmetric-routing, provider-maintenance.

cloud-support-bot: Provider case closed by slack note: They applied a permanent route-reflector fix in us-west2 and recommended we keep jittered timers; monitoring recommended for 24h.

maya (eng-network): final note: root cause = provider route-reflector race during maintenance + lack of automated local preference failover on our side + conntrack sticky sessions. Postmortem will include timelines, BGP dumps, and proposed actions.

jess (acct-mgr): customer follow-up sent with ETA for RCA (48h).

alex (oncall): closing pager. If anything regresses, reopen.

samir (sre): marking incident -> resolved (monitoring) in internal tracker.

incident-bot: Incident resolved at 1824510321."
